benefit.name: B.C. Sales Tax Credit
benefit.amount: Up to $75 for yourself and $75 for a cohabiting spouse or common-law partner
benefit.summary: A small refundable credit you claim on your tax return. It is not a disability program. It helps people with a low income who file a return.

items: You were a B.C. resident on December 31.
You were 19 or older, or had a spouse or common-law partner, or were a parent.

benefit.requiresNote: You were a B.C. resident on December 31 and were either 19 or older, or had a spouse or common-law partner, or were a parent.
benefit.note: The credit goes down by 2% of your net income over $15,000 if you are single. For couples, it goes down by 2% of family net income over $18,000. So it phases out at a low income. It is refundable up to the amount that is more than the income tax you owe. This means you can get it even if you owe no tax.

detail.about: Claim it when you file your T1 Income Tax Return using the British Columbia Credits form (BC479). You must claim within three years after the end of the tax year.
steps: File the federal T1 income tax return for the year
Complete the B.C. Credits form BC479
Enter the sales tax credit claim from BC479 with the return
If you missed it, ask the Canada Revenue Agency to adjust the return within three years after the tax year
documents: Tax slips and income information for the year
Spouse or common-law partner income information when applicable
tips: File even if you owe no income tax, because this credit is refundable
The credit depends on your income and is not only for people with disabilities
Ask the CRA if you have questions about the tax return and refund
detail.time: Claimed with the annual tax return
